extracted.intended_audience: clinicians and researchers writing/publishing medical case reports
extracted.subtask_description: A checklist for authors preparing clinical case reports, specifying the information to include (title, patient data, diagnostics, interventions, outcomes, discussion, patient perspective, and consent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: The diagnosis or intervention of primary focus followed by the words “case report”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the diagnosis or intervention of primary focus and append the phrase “case report” to the title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: 2 to 5 key words that identify diagnoses or interventions in this case report, including 'case report'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose 2–5 keywords that identify the key diagnoses or interventions; include the term 'case report' among keywords.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract (no references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an abstract without references. (Checklist header indicates abstract should be present; specific structured elements appear elsewhere such as introduction, patient information, clinical findings, timeline, diagnostic assessment, therapeutic intervention, follow-up and outcomes, discussion, patient perspective.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: What is unique about this case and what does it add to the scientific literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One or two paragraphs summarizing why this case is unique (may include references). State what the case adds to the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient Identification / De-identified patient information
rubrics_metrics.description: De-identified patient specific information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide patient-specific details necessary to understand the case while ensuring de-identification to protect privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary concerns and symptoms
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary concerns and symptoms of the patient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the presenting complaints and main symptoms that brought the patient to care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical, family, and psycho-social history
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical, family, and psycho-social history including relevant genetic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include relevant past medical history, family history, psychosocial context, and any pertinent genetic information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Past interventions with outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant past interventions with outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe previous treatments or interventions the patient received and their outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Findings / Physical Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe significant physical examination (PE) and important clinical findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report significant PE findings and other important clinical observations relevant to the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical and current information from this episode of care organized as a timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize key events, symptoms, tests, interventions, and outcomes in chronological order to show the course of the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic testing (such as PE, laboratory testing, imaging, surveys).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and summarize diagnostic tests performed (physical exam, labs, imaging, questionnaires), including results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic challenges (such as access to testing, financial, or cultural).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document any barriers or challenges that affected diagnosis (access, financial constraints, cultural issues, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnosis (including differential)
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnosis (including other diagnoses considered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the working/definitive diagnosis and list other diagnoses considered (differential).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prognosis
rubrics_metrics.description: Prognosis (such as staging in oncology) where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide prognosis information when applicable (for example staging, expected course, or prognostic indicators).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of therapeutic intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of therapeutic intervention (such as pharmacologic, surgical, preventive, self-care).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the category and nature of interventions used (medication, surgery, preventive measures, self-care, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration of therapeutic intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: Administration of therapeutic intervention (such as dosage, strength, duration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give practical details on how interventions were administered (dose, route, frequency, duration, device specifics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in therapeutic intervention (with rationale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in therapeutic intervention (with rationale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe any changes to interventions over time and explain the reasons for those changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinician and patient-assessed outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinician and patient-assessed outcomes (if available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report outcomes assessed both by clinicians and by the patient, if such assessments exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Important follow-up diagnostic and other test results
rubrics_metrics.description: Important follow-up diagnostic and other test results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include follow-up test results that demonstrate course or resolution of the condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention adherence and tolerability
rubrics_metrics.description: Intervention adherence and tolerability (How was this assessed?).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how adherence to the intervention was measured and report tolerability/adherence findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse and unanticipated events
rubrics_metrics.description: Adverse and unanticipated events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report any adverse events, complications, or unexpected outcomes related to interventions or the condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion — strengths and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A scientific discussion of the strengths AND limitations associated with this case report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a balanced appraisal of the case's strengths and limitations and their implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion — relevant literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the relevant medical literature with references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize the case within existing literature; cite relevant references to support discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion — scientific rationale for conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The scientific rationale for any conclusions (including assessment of possible causes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the reasoning behind conclusions, including possible causal inferences and supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion — primary take-away lessons
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary “take-away” lessons of this case report (without references) in a one paragraph conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize the main lessons or clinical points learned from the case in one paragraph, without references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient Perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: The patient should share their perspective in one to two paragraphs on the treatment(s) they received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include 1–2 paragraphs in the patient's own words describing their experience and perspective on care and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed Consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the patient give informed consent? Please provide if requested. (Yes / No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether informed consent was obtained from the patient and provide documentation if requested by the journal or publisher.
